title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - B-29
notes:
West leads the ♣5 against 3NT. South has 7 top tricks (3 spades, 2 hearts, the ♦A, and the ♣A). South can establish 2 more tricks in diamonds even if West has the ♦K and the finesse loses.

The only possible problem is that the defense might be in a position to cash 4 club tricks when West wins the ♦K. If South ducks the opening club lead, East may win the trick with a doubleton honour. East will return the suit and West will cash 3 more club tricks when he wins the ♦K.

South can virtually guarantee his contract by playing the ♣A at trick 1. If East has a doubleton honour, he can either play low, blocking the defensive clubs, or play high giving South a second stopper.

If the clubs were 4-3, the contract was never in danger. If West was dealt 5 clubs to the ♣K, ♣Q, and ♣J, he would have led the ♣K.
